messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a sustained uptick in spot churn in us-west-2 over the last 90m. Eviction rate jumped from ~1.2% to ~10% for gpus in the mixed pools. Some model routes started spiking latency as requests get re-routed.

liam: Ugh. Any idea if it's a single AZ or region-wide? Can you paste the query you used?

maya: Quick query I ran in grafana (approx):
```
sum by (az) (increase(eviction_events{pool="mixed-spot"}[15m])) / sum by (az) (increase(instance_count{pool="mixed-spot"}[15m]))
```
Numbers: us-west-2a ~12.3%, us-west-2b ~9.7%, us-west-2c ~11.0%. Baseline ~1.1% in us-east-1.

ops-bot: ALERT: spot-eviction-spike detected in us-west-2 (12:04 UTC). Auto-scaling buffers engaged.

arjun: Thanks. Two quick thoughts: (1) start routing non-critical / best-effort customers to a warm-spill lane in us-east-1, with soft drains in us-west-2 so we avoid mass requeueing; (2) enable model-variant degradation ladder for latency-sensitive routes — i.e. fall back from base fp16 -> quantized-4 -> quantized-8 smaller context variant rather than full region failover immediately.

sophia: Agree on the ladder. We need the cost math though — moving X% traffic cross-region adds egress + higher tail latency. I ran a micro-sim this morning: moving 20% of mixed-pool traffic to dedicated warm-standby (us-east) increases infra cost by ~18% but reduces 95p latency violations by ~72% under churn.

liam: Can we encode that in a routing policy? Something like:
```
- condition: eviction_rate(pool=mixed, region=us-west-2) > 5%
  action: promote: warm-standby(us-east-1) at weight: 0.15
  fallback: degradations: [quant4, quant8] per customer_tier: {free: quant8, standard: quant4, enterprise: base}
- condition: eviction_rate > 15%
  action: region-failover -> us-east-1
```
Would like the routing decision to prefer variant fallback before cross-region if customer_tier != enterprise.

arjun: That YAML looks fine. Two nitpicks: use moving-window averaged eviction_rate to avoid flapping, and add a cooldown per route: 5m. Also add a max-cross-region-traffic cap to avoid blowing egress.

maya: Agreed. Proposed policy we can push:
```
policy_name: soft-eviction-spill
window: 10m\nthresholds:\n  soft: 5%\n  hard: 15%\nactions:\n  - soft:\n      promote_warm_standby: 10%\n      variant_ladder: [quant4, quant8]\n      tier_overrides: {enterprise: skip_variant, standard: allow_variant, free: force_variant}\n  - hard:\n      failover_region: us-east-1\n      cap_cross_region: 30%\ncooldown: 5m\nuse_moving_avg: true
```
I'll draft the rollout in the console as a canary: 5% of affected routes first.

sophia: Please add a small experiment to measure end-to-end cost delta for 48h and the percent of requests hitting fallback variants vs region-failover. We need that telemetry to tune thresholds.

liam: SLA question — for enterprise customers we keep them pinned to dedicated pools where feasible. If pinned and not available, we should notify SRE and route to enterprise-warm only after explicit approval (or automatic after 10m).

maya: Noted. We'll add a pinned_exempt config for enterprise: {manual_escalation_window: 10m}. Also adding an alert to #oncall if pinned routes get soft-spilled.

arjun: One more: add a KV-cache affinity rule so warmed KV for a model variant is probed before traffic shifts. That reduces cold-start penalty when we spin up quantized variant nodes.

ops-bot: NOTE: rollout job created: soft-eviction-spill canary @ 05% for us-west-2 -> us-east-1. Job id: rollout-2026-03-18-191876.

maya: Thanks all. I'll push the canary, ops will watch the spike dashboard, and we'll reconvene in 30m unless things stabilize. :eyes:

liam: Sounds good. If churn persists after canary, we'll expand warm-standby + tweak thresholds.

sophia: Thx — I'll queue the cost experiment and a short dashboard for the variant hits.

maya: Oncall: please keep pager window open for next 2h.

ops-bot: oncall pager: arjun assigned.
